blocks.text: Dohra:
Then David Murry asked me once again, That I should reveal this secret also. How did the conflict come to develop, Between the Mughal emperors and the Sikh Gurus. (1)
lines: Then David Murry asked me once again,
That I should reveal this secret also.
How did the conflict come to develop,
Between the Mughal emperors and the Sikh Gurus.

blocks.text: Chaupai Then I explained to him the cause of this conflict between the two, And how the various Mughal emperors treated the Sikh Gurus.
How they kept on using the carrot and stick policy against the Gurus, But despite their shifting policies, they never abandoned their hostility. (2)
lines: How they kept on using the carrot and stick policy against the Gurus,
But despite their shifting policies, they never abandoned their hostility.

blocks.text: How when Aurangzeb took over the reins of power (at Delhi), He thought of committing a very sinful deed (against the Hindus). Which led to a direct conflict between him and Guru Tegh Bahadur, Which made both of them famous in the world for their deeds: Aurangzeb (for tyranny), Guru Tegh Bahadur (for sacrifice and human rights). (3)
lines: How when Aurangzeb took over the reins of power (at Delhi),
He thought of committing a very sinful deed (against the Hindus).
Which led to a direct conflict between him and Guru Tegh Bahadur,
Which made both of them famous in the world for their deeds: Aurangzeb (for tyranny),
Guru Tegh Bahadur (for sacrifice and human rights).

blocks.text: Dohra:
Aurangzeb had taken a vow in his mind, As soon as he descended to the throne of India. That he would convert all the Hindus to Muslims, After hunting the Hindus through out the twenty two states. (4)
lines: Aurangzeb had taken a vow in his mind,
As soon as he descended to the throne of India.
That he would convert all the Hindus to Muslims,
After hunting the Hindus through out the twenty two states.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Guru Tegh Bahadur came to be known as the bravest of the brave, As his fame spread far and wide in the whole world. Whosoever felt oppressed, tortured and aggrieved, Sought his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) protection and felt relieved. (5)
lines: Guru Tegh Bahadur came to be known as the bravest of the brave,
As his fame spread far and wide in the whole world.
Whosoever felt oppressed, tortured and aggrieved,
Sought his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) protection and felt relieved.

blocks.text: Human beings all over the world are desirous of comforts alone, They alone seek His grace who come across suffering in life. They received instant relief who sought his protection and, His fame spread all over the world for his alleviation of human suffering. (6)
lines: Human beings all over the world are desirous of comforts alone,
They alone seek His grace who come across suffering in life.
They received instant relief who sought his protection and,
His fame spread all over the world for his alleviation of human suffering.

blocks.text: Dohra:
This fact came to light through out the world, That he (Guru Tegh Bahadur) was a true prophet. Whosoever came to seek his protection, He got relieved and redeemed. (7)
lines: This fact came to light through out the world,
That he (Guru Tegh Bahadur) was a true prophet.
Whosoever came to seek his protection,
He got relieved and redeemed.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

So when the Muslim writ began to run all over the country, They planned to convert the Hindus through a witch-hunt. Then the Hindus felt extremely concerned at this development, And they arrived at a resolution after thorough deliberations. (8)
lines: So when the Muslim writ began to run all over the country,
They planned to convert the Hindus through a witch-hunt.
Then the Hindus felt extremely concerned at this development,
And they arrived at a resolution after thorough deliberations.

blocks.text: That they should leave this problem to be dealt by the Brahmins2 , As they might succeed in getting some providential reprieve for them. Thereupon the poor, helpless Hindus went with folded hands, And stood before Aurangzeb in humble supplication. (9)
lines: That they should leave this problem to be dealt by the Brahmins2 ,
As they might succeed in getting some providential reprieve for them.
Thereupon the poor, helpless Hindus went with folded hands,
And stood before Aurangzeb in humble supplication.

blocks.text: They remarked since they were in subordination of the Brahmins, The Emperor should first convert the Brahmins to Islam. Thereafter, they would also accept Islam after their peers, This is how the poor Hindu populace played a trick with the Brahmins. (10)
lines: They remarked since they were in subordination of the Brahmins,
The Emperor should first convert the Brahmins to Islam.
Thereafter, they would also accept Islam after their peers,
This is how the poor Hindu populace played a trick with the Brahmins.

blocks.text: Thus these poorer Hindus got themselves absolved of this threat, And shifted the whole responsibility to the Brahmins. Thereafter the emperor Aurangzeb summoned the Brahmins, And ordered them to get converted to Islam. (11)
lines: Thus these poorer Hindus got themselves absolved of this threat,
And shifted the whole responsibility to the Brahmins.
Thereafter the emperor Aurangzeb summoned the Brahmins,
And ordered them to get converted to Islam.

blocks.text: He promised them all the perks and privileges of their choice, If they changed their religion and converted to Islam. Otherwise, all of them would be exiled from the country, And persecuted to death if they dared to stay there. (12)
lines: He promised them all the perks and privileges of their choice,
If they changed their religion and converted to Islam.
Otherwise, all of them would be exiled from the country,
And persecuted to death if they dared to stay there.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing this proclamation, they turned pale and bloodless, As if all of their families had perished in one stroke. They would have gladly escaped to any non-Muslim country, But all the surrounding countries were inhabited with the Muslims. (13)
lines: Hearing this proclamation, they turned pale and bloodless,
As if all of their families had perished in one stroke.
They would have gladly escaped to any non-Muslim country,
But all the surrounding countries were inhabited with the Muslims.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thus, the Brahmins came under great stress and adversity, Day and Night, they were at their wits' ends to find a solution. Finally, they prayed for a few days reprieve and postponement, With a view to find some way out of this ordeal. (14)
lines: Thus, the Brahmins came under great stress and adversity,
Day and Night, they were at their wits' ends to find a solution.
Finally, they prayed for a few days reprieve and postponement,
With a view to find some way out of this ordeal.

blocks.text: Thereafter, the Brahmins meditated and fasted to invoke their gods, But no gods or goddess came to their help despite their rigorous invocations. In the meantime, some slanderers reported against them, That they (Brahmins) were trying to cast some magic spells. (15)
lines: Thereafter, the Brahmins meditated and fasted to invoke their gods,
But no gods or goddess came to their help despite their rigorous invocations.
In the meantime, some slanderers reported against them,
That they (Brahmins) were trying to cast some magic spells.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing about this alleged mischief by the Brahmins, Aurangzeb felt extremely infuriated against them. He ordered all the Hindus (mostly Brahmins) from Kashmir to be converted, And proclaimed that their religion (Hinduism) be wiped out from there. (16)
lines: Hearing about this alleged mischief by the Brahmins,
Aurangzeb felt extremely infuriated against them.
He ordered all the Hindus (mostly Brahmins) from Kashmir to be converted,
And proclaimed that their religion (Hinduism) be wiped out from there.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

He dispatched Horse-mounted soldiers to the Kashmir valley, And they ran posthaste towards Kashmir on receiving orders. They caught hold of all the Hindus forcibly under duress, And converted all of them to Islam. (17)
lines: He dispatched Horse-mounted soldiers to the Kashmir valley,
And they ran posthaste towards Kashmir on receiving orders.
They caught hold of all the Hindus forcibly under duress,
And converted all of them to Islam.

blocks.text: Despite all the desperate efforts of the Hindus to escape and hide, All of them were made to convert to Islam by force. When these mass-scale conversions terrified the whole country, The Brahmins approached Satguru (Guru Tegh Bahadur) for protection. (18)
lines: Despite all the desperate efforts of the Hindus to escape and hide,
All of them were made to convert to Islam by force.
When these mass-scale conversions terrified the whole country,
The Brahmins approached Satguru (Guru Tegh Bahadur) for protection.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Brahmins from all the nooks and corners of the country, From Kashi (Benaras), Gangetic plains, Kurukshetra and other places. Assembled together and prepared a joint petition, And presented it to Guru Tegh Bahadur to save their religion. (19)
lines: The Brahmins from all the nooks and corners of the country,
From Kashi (Benaras),
Gangetic plains,
Kurukshetra and other places.
Assembled together and prepared a joint petition,
And presented it to Guru Tegh Bahadur to save their religion.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

In this way, they approached and petitioned to Guru Tegh Bahadur, And sought his protection, considering him the true embodiment of the Divine. Acknowledging him to be the Divinely annointed warrior (Kshatriya3 ), They beseeched him to protect the dignity of their religion and faith. (20)
lines: In this way, they approached and petitioned to Guru Tegh Bahadur,
And sought his protection, considering him the true embodiment of the Divine.
Acknowledging him to be the Divinely annointed warrior (Kshatriya3 ),
They beseeched him to protect the dignity of their religion and faith.

blocks.text: Since they had fallen on bad days in this hour of misery, Guru Tegh Bahadur must stand by them in their hour of trial. Being a true and revealed prophet (Satguru) of the House of Nanak, He must protect the honour of the Hindus in their hour of trial. (21)
lines: Since they had fallen on bad days in this hour of misery,
Guru Tegh Bahadur must stand by them in their hour of trial.
Being a true and revealed prophet (Satguru) of the House of Nanak,
He must protect the honour of the Hindus in their hour of trial.

blocks.text: That all the Hindus were to be completely eliminated from India (Hindustan), The Emperor Aurangzeb made a proclamation to that effect. All the Brahmins were to be converted in the first attempt, Rest of the Hindus were to be dealt with after that. (22)
lines: That all the Hindus were to be completely eliminated from India (Hindustan),
The Emperor Aurangzeb made a proclamation to that effect.
All the Brahmins were to be converted in the first attempt,
Rest of the Hindus were to be dealt with after that.

blocks.text: Since the Brahmins were the leaders of all the Hindus, Conversion of the Brahmins will lead to everyone else's conversion to Islam. This being the declared policy of the Emperor Aurangzeb, And being threatened by it, the Brahmins came to seek his protection. (23)
lines: Since the Brahmins were the leaders of all the Hindus,
Conversion of the Brahmins will lead to everyone else's conversion to Islam.
This being the declared policy of the Emperor Aurangzeb,
And being threatened by it, the Brahmins came to seek his protection.

blocks.text: If Guru Tegh Bahadur was a perfect prophet and a supreme warrior, Then he must protect all the Hindus of India. Otherwise they would name him (Guru Tegh Bahadur) to be converted first, After him, they would voluntarily embrace Islam. (24)
lines: If Guru Tegh Bahadur was a perfect prophet and a supreme warrior,
Then he must protect all the Hindus of India.
Otherwise they would name him (Guru Tegh Bahadur) to be converted first,
After him, they would voluntarily embrace Islam.

blocks.text: They entreated him to pick up a sword like a brave Kshtriya, And win the hearts of all the Hindus of the whole country. As Guru Tegh Bahadur alone had lots of financial resources, And unlimited spiritual powers to combat this challenge. (25)
lines: They entreated him to pick up a sword like a brave Kshtriya,
And win the hearts of all the Hindus of the whole country.
As Guru Tegh Bahadur alone had lots of financial resources,
And unlimited spiritual powers to combat this challenge.

blocks.text: Dohra:

The Hindus were ten times more in numerical strength, Than that of Muslims in the whole of India (Hindustan). If Guru Tegh Bahadur picked up a sword against the Muslims, All the Hindus would rally round him in this fight. (26)
lines: The Hindus were ten times more in numerical strength,
Than that of Muslims in the whole of India (Hindustan).
If Guru Tegh Bahadur picked up a sword against the Muslims,
All the Hindus would rally round him in this fight.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Guru Nanak had made a prediction in his own words and, Blessed the Muslims to wield the sword but not for committing oppression. Otherwise he would destroy the Muslims with his own sacrifice, Such was the blessing and prediction of Guru Nanak. (27)
lines: Guru Nanak had made a prediction in his own words and,
Blessed the Muslims to wield the sword but not for committing oppression.
Otherwise he would destroy the Muslims with his own sacrifice,
Such was the blessing and prediction of Guru Nanak.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Guru Tegh Bahadur remarked if it benefitted the Hindus, He would not hesitate for a second to offer his sacrifice, Which would not only uproot the tyrannical Muslim rule, But would get them (the Muslims) even damned in the House of the true Lord/God. (28)
lines: Guru Tegh Bahadur remarked if it benefitted the Hindus,
He would not hesitate for a second to offer his sacrifice,
Which would not only uproot the tyrannical Muslim rule,
But would get them (the Muslims) even damned in the House of the true Lord/God.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

The Brahmins responded to Guru Tegh Bahadur's offer somewhat like this: That his sacrifice would take long to uproot the Muslim tyranny. As the Muslims were hell-bent on converting the Brahmin's faith in a year A mere offer of sacrifice would not save their honour. (29)
lines: The Brahmins responded to Guru Tegh Bahadur's offer somewhat like this: That his sacrifice would take long to uproot the Muslim tyranny.
As the Muslims were hell-bent on converting the Brahmin's faith in a year A mere offer of sacrifice would not save their honour.

blocks.text: What purpose would the offer of a boat serve for the drowned, How could an offer of food revive a person dead of starvation? How could a dip in water bring back a person dead of dehydration, to life, Whose thirst could water quench after a person's death? (30)
lines: What purpose would the offer of a boat serve for the drowned,
How could an offer of food revive a person dead of starvation?
How could a dip in water bring back a person dead of dehydration, to life,
Whose thirst could water quench after a person's death?

blocks.text: Dohra:

Then Guru Tegh Bahadur told the Brahmins in this vein, To rid them of the gnawing fear of their persecution. They should tell Aurangzeb to convert Guru Tegh Bahadur to Islam first, After whose conversion they would also accept Islam. (31)
lines: Then Guru Tegh Bahadur told the Brahmins in this vein,
To rid them of the gnawing fear of their persecution.
They should tell Aurangzeb to convert Guru Tegh Bahadur to Islam first,
After whose conversion they would also accept Islam.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thereafter, the Brahmins reported to Aurangzeb in the same vein, In which they were advised by Guru Tegh Bahadur. That he should first convert Guru Tegh Bahadur to Islam, After that, all the citizens of India (Hindustan) would follow him. (32)
lines: Thereafter, the Brahmins reported to Aurangzeb in the same vein,
In which they were advised by Guru Tegh Bahadur.
That he should first convert Guru Tegh Bahadur to Islam,
After that, all the citizens of India (Hindustan) would follow him.

blocks.text: So the wily Brahmins fed this information into Emperor's ears, Who accepted it as an authentic version without any verification. And Aurangzeb started stalking after Guru Tegh Bahadur's movements, He dispatched his officials to hunt Guru Tegh Bahadur Down. (33)
lines: So the wily Brahmins fed this information into Emperor's ears,
Who accepted it as an authentic version without any verification.
And Aurangzeb started stalking after Guru Tegh Bahadur's movements,
He dispatched his officials to hunt Guru Tegh Bahadur Down.

blocks.text: On the other hand, Guru Tegh Bahadur made preparations to fulfill his promise, As he had made it out to the supplicating Brahmins. So Guru Tegh Bahadur marched towards Delhi on his own, And offered himself for arrest before the Muslim ruler. (34)
lines: On the other hand,
Guru Tegh Bahadur made preparations to fulfill his promise,
As he had made it out to the supplicating Brahmins.
So Guru Tegh Bahadur marched towards Delhi on his own,
And offered himself for arrest before the Muslim ruler.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus standing in front of the entrance to the walled city of Delhi, Guru Tegh Bahadur sent a messenger with an expensive garment4 (Doshala). Who placed it at a sweetmeat seller's shop to buy some sweets, This was a mere ploy to make his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) whereabouts known. (35)
lines: Thus standing in front of the entrance to the walled city of Delhi,
Guru Tegh Bahadur sent a messenger with an expensive garment4 (Doshala).
Who placed it at a sweetmeat seller's shop to buy some sweets,
This was a mere ploy to make his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) whereabouts known.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Aurangzeb took all the credit for Guru's arrest and made it public, That Guru Tegh Bahadur had been arrested in Delhi. This is how Guru Tegh Bahadur got into Aurangzeb's custody, This is how he offered himself for arrest before Aurangzeb. (36)
lines: Aurangzeb took all the credit for Guru's arrest and made it public,
That Guru Tegh Bahadur had been arrested in Delhi.
This is how Guru Tegh Bahadur got into Aurangzeb's custody,
This is how he offered himself for arrest before Aurangzeb.

blocks.text: After taking into custody, the Guru was subjected to severe tortures, Thereafter, a Muslim messenger was sent to communicate with him. Using abusive language, the messenger threatened him with dire consequences, If Guru Tegh Bahadur did not convert to Islam. (37)
lines: After taking into custody, the Guru was subjected to severe tortures,
Thereafter, a Muslim messenger was sent to communicate with him.
Using abusive language, the messenger threatened him with dire consequences,
If Guru Tegh Bahadur did not convert to Islam.

blocks.text: Otherwise, he should bring about certain miracles and marvels, As he claimed himself to be a Guru or a prophet. As he was known to be a 'Sacha Patshah'5 , a Divine Prophet, And he had been branding the Mughal Emperor a false emperor. (38)
lines: Otherwise, he should bring about certain miracles and marvels,
As he claimed himself to be a Guru or a prophet.
As he was known to be a 'Sacha Patshah'5 , a Divine Prophet,
And he had been branding the Mughal Emperor a false emperor.

blocks.text: Either Guru Tegh Bahadur should convert himself to Islam, Or he should display some miracles with all his spiritual powers. He must make a show of his miraculous powers before them, As his ancestor Ram Rai had displayed certain miracles. (39)
lines: Either Guru Tegh Bahadur should convert himself to Islam,
Or he should display some miracles with all his spiritual powers.
He must make a show of his miraculous powers before them,
As his ancestor Ram Rai had displayed certain miracles.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Hearing upon this, Guru Tegh Bahadur made this remark: That Ram Rai had not done a noble deed with the display of miracles, Although he earned a cheap reputation for himself, But he had set a bad precedent for his successors. (40)
lines: Hearing upon this,
Guru Tegh Bahadur made this remark: That Ram Rai had not done a noble deed with the display of miracles,
Although he earned a cheap reputation for himself,
But he had set a bad precedent for his successors.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Ram Rai6 by making a show of his miraculous powers, To which the Muslim Messenger had made a reference, Had committed a sinful deed unbecoming of spiritual saints, And thus damaged the spiritual credibility of all saints. (41)
lines: Ram Rai6 by making a show of his miraculous powers,
To which the Muslim Messenger had made a reference,
Had committed a sinful deed unbecoming of spiritual saints,
And thus damaged the spiritual credibility of all saints.

blocks.text: All spiritual personages do not make a show of miracles, But the Mughal administration would not let off a saint without miracles. He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) would not display any miraculous feats, So that it might not become a liability for the later saints (42)
lines: All spiritual personages do not make a show of miracles,
But the Mughal administration would not let off a saint without miracles.
He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) would not display any miraculous feats,
So that it might not become a liability for the later saints

blocks.text: Since Display of miracles is a violation of Nature's laws and a curse for humanity, Both spiritual saints and emperors should desist from this temptation. As both the supremes (spiritual and temporal) were meant to alleviate human suffering, So why should spiritual saints bring about such a disaster? (43)
lines: Since Display of miracles is a violation of Nature's laws and a curse for humanity,
Both spiritual saints and emperors should desist from this temptation.
As both the supremes (spiritual and temporal) were meant to alleviate human suffering,
So why should spiritual saints bring about such a disaster?

blocks.text: Dohra:

Considering display of Miraculous feats to be synonymous with disaster, He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) refused to make a display of any miracles. And permitted Aurangzeb to commit any atrocity on him (Guru Tegh Bahadur), For which he would be held accountable by God. (44)
lines: Considering display of Miraculous feats to be synonymous with disaster,
He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) refused to make a display of any miracles.
And permitted Aurangzeb to commit any atrocity on him (Guru Tegh Bahadur),
For which he would be held accountable by God.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

At this remark, Aurangzeb feeling extremely infuriated, Accused Guru Tegh Bahadur of making his escape through polemics. He warned the Guru to either get converted to Islam, Or he must be prepared to face death through execution. (45)
lines: At this remark,
Aurangzeb feeling extremely infuriated,
Accused Guru Tegh Bahadur of making his escape through polemics.
He warned the Guru to either get converted to Islam,
Or he must be prepared to face death through execution.

blocks.text: He (Aurangzeb) would have his body sewn in a cover of raw leather, And then he would put up his sealed body in the sun to dry up. As the raw leather containing his body would dry and tighten, He would have to bear the torture of a squeezed leather grip. (46)
lines: He (Aurangzeb) would have his body sewn in a cover of raw leather,
And then he would put up his sealed body in the sun to dry up.
As the raw leather containing his body would dry and tighten,
He would have to bear the torture of a squeezed leather grip.

blocks.text: Accusing him of wearing the mantle of a prophet, and exploiting the masses, How could he now escape to embrace Islam after that? Were the Muslims not as similar human beings as the Hindus, Why did the Hindus have such contempt for the Muslims? (47)
lines: Accusing him of wearing the mantle of a prophet, and exploiting the masses,
How could he now escape to embrace Islam after that?
Were the Muslims not as similar human beings as the Hindus,
Why did the Hindus have such contempt for the Muslims?

blocks.text: Thereupon Satguru (Guru Tegh Bahadur) deliberated upon the whole situation, And concluded that the moment for shedding his mortal frame had arrived. The much-awaited moment for which he had been waiting, That moment of truth had arrived in his life. (Thus accepting God's Will) he recited the following hymn: "One should feel concerned about those things alone, Which occur unexpectedly or unnaturally. Nanak says that in this world of change and flux, Nothing is permanent and eternal." (48)
lines: Thereupon Satguru (Guru Tegh Bahadur) deliberated upon the whole situation,
And concluded that the moment for shedding his mortal frame had arrived.
The much-awaited moment for which he had been waiting,
That moment of truth had arrived in his life.
(Thus accepting God's Will) he recited the following hymn: "One should feel concerned about those things alone,
Which occur unexpectedly or unnaturally.
Nanak says that in this world of change and flux,
Nothing is permanent and eternal."

blocks.text: Dohra:
So Satguru, Guru Tegh Bahadur came to realize, That the moment of truth had arrived indeed. He should no longer delay his resolution, And should come forward to make a supreme sacrifice. (49)
lines: So Satguru,
Guru Tegh Bahadur came to realize,
That the moment of truth had arrived indeed.
He should no longer delay his resolution,
And should come forward to make a supreme sacrifice.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Then Guru Tegh Bahadur addressed Aurangzeb in this vein, That he would now have a glimpse of his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) spiritual powers. He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) would bring about such a miracle, That he (Aurangzeb) would never be able to get hold of his (Guru Tegh Bahadur 's) head.(50)
lines: Then Guru Tegh Bahadur addressed Aurangzeb in this vein,
That he would now have a glimpse of his (Guru Tegh Bahadur's) spiritual powers.
He (Guru Tegh Bahadur) would bring about such a miracle,
That he (Aurangzeb) would never be able to get hold of his (Guru Tegh Bahadur 's) head.

blocks.text: Whichever sword he may choose to severe his head with, But will it not be a miracle if it failed to cut through his throat. So he might arrange for the sharpest sword for executing him, Because an ordinary sword used for daily executions might not work. (51)
lines: Whichever sword he may choose to severe his head with,
But will it not be a miracle if it failed to cut through his throat.
So he might arrange for the sharpest sword for executing him,
Because an ordinary sword used for daily executions might not work.

blocks.text: Dohra:

After addressing the emperor in these words, Guru Tegh Bahadur sat on the executioner's slab after ablutions. Guru Tegh Bahadur made the executioners' sword just touch his head, But it was just a ploy to hoodwink the authorities (52)
lines: After addressing the emperor in these words,
Guru Tegh Bahadur sat on the executioner's slab after ablutions.
Guru Tegh Bahadur made the executioners' sword just touch his head,
But it was just a ploy to hoodwink the authorities

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thus Guru Tegh Bahadur made the supreme sacrifice without compromising his dignity, And protected both his religion as well its practices. Not only he saved his body from being sewn in raw leather, But also laid the blame of execution squarely on the Muslims. (53)
lines: Thus Guru Tegh Bahadur made the supreme sacrifice without compromising his dignity,
And protected both his religion as well its practices.
Not only he saved his body from being sewn in raw leather,
But also laid the blame of execution squarely on the Muslims.

blocks.text: The foolish Muslim rulers did not realize their stupidity, That the Guru was determined to lay the blame on their head. Thus, Guru Tegh Bahadur had made the supreme sacrifice, He had sacrificed his life for the protection of others' rights. (54)
lines: The foolish Muslim rulers did not realize their stupidity,
That the Guru was determined to lay the blame on their head.
Thus,
Guru Tegh Bahadur had made the supreme sacrifice,
He had sacrificed his life for the protection of others' rights.

blocks.text: An Illustration from Bachittar Natak7
Dohra:

"Leaving his Mortal frame and laying the blame squarely on the Delhi ruler, Sri Guru Tegh Bahadur departed for his heavenly abode. He had made such a supreme sacrifice, That none else could accomplish such a deed. After Guru Tegh Bahadur departed for his heavenly abode, The whole world was plunged into grief and gloom. While the entire humanity raised a cry of helplersness, The heavens above reverberated with the shouts of victory."
Dohra:

Satguru brought about such a miracle through his sacrifice, That the Muslim ruler felt extremely exasperated. Aurangzeb cried out in utter repentance and remorse, That he could not visualize the real import of such a miraculous deed. (55)
lines: Satguru brought about such a miracle through his sacrifice,
That the Muslim ruler felt extremely exasperated.
Aurangzeb cried out in utter repentance and remorse,
That he could not visualize the real import of such a miraculous deed.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

(After Guru's sacrifice), Aurangzeb felt so much frightened, That he stopped his oppression and tyranny against the Hindus. Peace and patience came to prevail all around, The people's outcry had rent the God's portals. (56)
lines: (After Guru's sacrifice),
Aurangzeb felt so much frightened,
That he stopped his oppression and tyranny against the Hindus.
Peace and patience came to prevail all around,
The people's outcry had rent the God's portals.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Mankind's cries reverberated in the House of God, Which made Him contemplate over mankind's woes. As a result, all the Pirs and prophets belonging to Islam, Were turned out of the heavenly abode of God. (57)
lines: Mankind's cries reverberated in the House of God,
Which made Him contemplate over mankind's woes.
As a result, all the Pirs and prophets belonging to Islam,
Were turned out of the heavenly abode of God.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

After having been turned out of God's heavenly abode, They were rehabilitated on the back yard of heaven. Thereafter, the Mughal's grip over Delhi's throne loosened, And their political power to rule over India also declined. (58)
lines: After having been turned out of God's heavenly abode,
They were rehabilitated on the back yard of heaven.
Thereafter, the Mughal's grip over Delhi's throne loosened,
And their political power to rule over India also declined.
